(a) Evidence. With respect to all hearings before the board or the hearing officer/panel under this division, the following rules regarding the evidence shall govern:
(1) Formal, legal rules of evidence shall not be strictly applied. Evidence may be admitted if it is of a type commonly relied upon by reasonably prudent persons in the conduct of their affairs. The hearing officer/panel shall follow the state rules of evidence regarding privileges, recognized by the law of the state.
(2) Irrelevant, immaterial or unduly repetitious evidence may be excluded.
(3) Objections to evidentiary offers may be made and shall be noted in the record.
(4) When a hearing will be expedited and the interest of the parties will not be prejudiced substantially, any part of the evidence may be received in written form, including but not limited to the use of depositions or interrogatories.
(5) Documentary evidence may be received in the form of copies if the original is not readily available. Upon request and at the discretion of the hearing officer/panel, parties shall be given the opportunity to compare the copy with the original document.
(b) Attendance at hearing. Upon the motion of either party, the hearing officer/panel may close the hearing of any appeal under this article, as provided by O.C.G.A. § 50-14-3(6), or by any federal privacy statute. An appeal file containing evidence received in a closed hearing shall not be included in a public record.
(Ord. No. 010-08, § 3, 3-17-08)
277:
(a) Requirements of decision. As part of the final decision, the hearing officer/panel shall include findings of fact and any law on which the decision is based, separately stated, and the effective date of the decision or order. Findings of fact shall be accompanied by a concise and explicit statement of the underlying facts supporting the findings. Copies of the decision or order shall be mailed to all parties of record by the city manager.
(b) Finality of decision. The decision of the hearing officer/panel shall be binding on both parties. The hearing officer/panel may modify the adverse action of the appointing authority but may not increase the severity of such action on the employee. The appointing authority shall promptly comply with the final decision as may be issued as a result of the appeal.
(c) Relief of employee. If the decision of the hearing officer/panel is in favor of the employee on appeals of dismissal, suspension or demotion, the employee shall be reinstated in accordance with the decision to the classification from which the employee was removed. The effective date of the reinstatement shall be the date immediately following the effective date of the appealed action as if there had been no break in service, unless otherwise specified in the order. The employee shall be entitled to the same salary, with any increments in the position or salary which would have automatically inured to the employee if the employee had remained in actual service. The employee shall receive payment as if there had been no break in service, minus any amount earned by or paid to the employee from other employment and wage substitutions, including but not limited to unemployment compensation, during the period off the job and minus any amount paid the employee for annual leave. Sick and annual leave shall be restored to the employee in the same amount that existed at the time of the appealed action, plus sick and annual leave that would have been earned for the period if the employee had actually been in service. However, any period of postponement or continuance of the hearing for the convenience of the employee shall be excluded from any payment of benefits due, and this period of time shall be considered as if the employee had been on leave without pay. Prior to any payment to the employee, the employee shall certify under oath the amount of any income received from other employment and any wage substitutes received during the period off the job, which shall be deducted from the backpay owed by the city.
(d) The decision of the hearing officer/panel under this division shall not limit the right of either party to judicial review, and such decision shall be stayed by the filing of a petition for review. Any party, including the city or any city department, who has exhausted all administrative remedies available before the board and who is aggrieved by a final decision or order of the board on any hearing may seek judicial review of the final decision or order of the board in the superior court of Fulton County by writ of certiorari.
(Ord. No. 010-08, § 3, 3-17-08)

285:
(a) Employees of the city are encouraged to exercise their right to vote, but no employee shall make use of city time or equipment to aid a political candidate, political party or political cause or use a city position to persuade, coerce or intimidate any person in the interest of a political candidate, political party or political cause.
(b) Any employee who has qualified or seeks to qualify for any elected office shall comply with the following provisions:
(1) Within three (3) days of qualifying, notify the personnel director and file a statement indicating what steps the candidate will take to assure that no city time, resources or equipment will be used to assist in the campaign and what steps will be taken to meet the employee's job responsibilities if elected.
(2) Provide notice to the personnel director, city manager and city council of his qualification or intent to qualify and seek elective office, together with the office to which election is sought.
(3) Provide notice of the date the employee will take leave of absence by vacation or leave without pay in the event insufficient accumulated vacation time is available to the employee. In the event any city employee is seeking an office should succeed to a runoff election, the leave of absence hereinabove provided shall extend through the period of time of any such runoff election or primary runoff.

(6) In the event a city employee is elected to an office having legislative or other regulatory powers or jurisdiction over the governing authority of the city, or an elected position with any political body or entity which, at the time of election, has any contractual relationship with the city, notwithstanding the provisions of subparagraph (b)(5) above, the employee shall be required to resign employment with the city effective as of the date of taking office or the position to which such employee is elected or in any other manner assuming the responsibilities of said elective position or office. In the event, during the interim period of time from election to taking office, the city manager is not satisfied that the employee will not be devoting any portion of his time in his capacity as an employee of the city to said elected post, the city manager, after obtaining the concurrence of the governing authority of the city, may require such employee to resign from employment with the city immediately upon such determination by the city manager with the concurrence of the governing authority of the city. The classification plan is the systematic grouping of positions into appropriate classes.
(1) A position is a group of current assigned duties and responsibilities requiring the full or part time employment of one person. A position may be occupied or vacant.
(2) A class is a group of positions (or one position) that:
a. Has similar duties and responsibilities;
b. Requires like qualifications; and
c. Can be equitably compensated by the same range of pay.
(3) The class title is the official designation or name of the class, and it shall be used on all personnel records and transactions.
287: Specifications are to be interpreted in their entirety and in relation to others in the classification plan. Particular phrases or examples are not to be isolated and treated as a full definition of a class. Specifications are descriptive and explanatory of the kind of work performed and not necessarily inclusive of all duties performed.
288: The personnel director, under the direction of the city manager, shall maintain the classification plan so that it will reflect the duties performed by each employee in the classified service. He or she shall periodically review the entire classification plan and recommend appropriate changes in allocations or in the classification plan. Reclassification shall not be abused or used to impose disciplinary action upon an employee.
289: When a new position is established, or duties of an existing position change, the department head involved shall submit in writing a position description stating the duties and responsibilities of the position. The personnel director shall investigate the actual or proposed duties and recommend to the city manager the appropriate class allocation or the establishment of a new class. The city manager then shall approve or change the recommendations and allocate the position to a class.
290: An employee who considers his position improperly classified shall submit his reclassification request, in writing, to his supervisor who shall make a recommendation to the personnel director within seven (7) days of receipt of the appeal. The personnel director shall proceed as outlined in section 4-1030 of this article.
291: The classification plan shall be considered a part of this section and shall have the same force and effect as these personnel rules and regulations. A certified copy of the classification plan shall be maintained by the personnel director and filed with the city clerk.
292:

293: The pay plan includes the adopted salary schedule and the schedule of salary ranges consisting of rates of pay for all classes of positions included in the classification plan.

305:
(a) The personnel director shall review all applications for employment to determine whether the applicant meets the established standards for employment. The information may be required as is necessary to make such determination. When appropriate, examinations may be used which may be written or oral or a combination of these. The tests shall be practical in character and shall relate to the duties and responsibilities of the position for which the applicant is being examined.
(b) Applicants meeting the employment standards will be referred to the employing department head by the personnel director. The personnel director may reasonably limit the number of applicants referred to the department head; however, the department head may request that all applications of persons applying for the job be referred to him. The department head shall make a selection from the applicants referred and shall notify the personnel director of his recommendation as soon as he makes a decision.
306:
The city manager or personnel director shall review and either accept or reject the recommendation of the department head as to the applicant to be employed. If the applicant recommended by the department head is rejected, the department head shall make another recommendation to the city manager or personnel director. Upon the failure or refusal of the department head to make a recommendation, or another recommendation if previous recommendation is rejected, the city manager may select the person considered to be the most qualified to fill the position for employment with the city. When an applicant is selected, the city manager or personnel director shall authorize or direct an offer of employment.
(Ord. No. 751-81, § 1, 8-17-81)
307: When an emergency involving the serious impairment of the public business makes it impossible to fill a vacant position by normal procedure, the department head, with the approval of the personnel director and the city manager, may appoint any qualified person to the position on a temporary basis in order to prevent stoppage of public business or loss, or serious inconvenience to the public. Such an appointment shall be for a period not to exceed thirty-one (31) days during which time the normal selection procedures would be followed in order to fill the position permanently.
308: Editor's note— Ord. No. 032-08, § 1, adopted Nov. 17, 2008, repealed former § 4-1048.1 in its entirety which pertained to the employment of deemed retirees and derived from Ord. No. 005-04, § 1, adopted Feb. 16, 2004.
309:
It has been determined to be in the best interest of, and is therefore the policy of the city not to employ any person in a position in which such person directly supervises, or is directly supervised by, a member of an employee's immediate family. As used herein, "immediate family" shall mean any person holding a relationship with a present employee of the city of husband, wife, son, daughter, brother or sister, and to father, mother, father-in-law, mother-in-law, sister-in-law, brother-in-law, son-in-law, or daughter-in-law. This policy applies to promotions, demotions, transfers, reinstatements and new employees.
(1) If two (2) employees marry while working with the city then one shall not thereafter be in a supervisory capacity over the other. If two (2) employees are married and one is in a supervisory capacity over the other or attains a supervisory position while working in the same department, one must transfer, within thirty (30) days of the date of their marriage, to another department, if both are to continue working for the city. Subject to the approval of the city manager, the two (2) employees may agree which would prefer to transfer. In the event the city manager does not approve the agreement between the two (2) employees, or the two (2) employees are not able to agree upon which should transfer, the employee with the shortest seniority in the department will be required to transfer. In the event there has been no position available for transfer at the end of the thirty (30) days, the transferring employee shall be required to take a leave of absence without pay, unless such employee has accrued vacation or compensatory time, and shall have five (5) months thereafter within which to effectuate such transfer to the first available position. If said additional five-month period expires without said transferring employee transferring to another position, all continued rights of employment shall cease. If or when said transferring employee is on a leave without pay pending transfer, all benefits of the city shall cease during the period of said leave and not recommence thereafter until such transferring employee resumes employment with the city.
(2) If a city institutes a reorganization which changes departmental boundaries where immediate family members would be supervising or is directly supervised by, another member of his or her immediate family, one of such employees must transfer to another department within thirty (30) days of the date of the reorganization if both are to continue working with the city. Subject to the approval of the city manager, the two (2) employees may agree which would prefer to transfer. In the event the city manager does not approve the agreement between the two (2) employees, or the two (2) employees are unable to agree upon which should transfer, the employee in the lowest pay grade in the new department will be required to transfer. If in the event there has been no position available for transfer at the end of the thirty (30) days, the transferring employee shall be transferred to any position designated by the city manager, to the highest pay grade available for such position, if such transfer results in a reduction in pay for such individual; provided, that said transferring employee's pay does not exceed the pay of an employee in the lower pay grade with like seniority of the transferring employee. Thereafter, the transferring employee may transfer to any other department in the city provided said employee may not resume a position in the department wherein an immediate family member holds a supervisory position.
(Ord. No. 802-82, § 1, 8-16-82; Ord. No. 969-88, § 1, 8-15-88)
310: The probationary period shall be regarded as an integral part of the selection process and shall be utilized for closely observing the employee's work, for securing the most effective adjustment of a new employee to this position and for rejecting any employee whose performance is not satisfactory. Employees serving their probationary period do not have appeal rights unless there is alleged discrimination because of political affiliation, religious affiliation, race, age, color, creed, sex, national origin, ancestry or disability. Employees who are separated from the city service prior to the completion of their probationary service shall receive no vacation pay.
311: The probationary period shall be for a minimum of six (6) months to a maximum of twelve (12) months. The length of the probationary period for each class shall be established by the personnel director with the approval of the city manager. If a department head requests an extension of an established probationary period prior to fifteen (15) days before expiration, the personnel director, with the approval of the city manager, may extend the probationary period of a particular employee up to three (3) months beyond the end of the normal probationary period.
312: After the employee has completed one-half of his established probationary period, the department head shall report to the personnel director, in writing, his observation of the employee's work and his judgment as to whether or not the employee's services have been satisfactory. During the probationary period, the employee's supervisor will tell the employee when he is not performing satisfactorily. At least fifteen (15) days prior to the expiration of an employee's probationary period, the department head shall notify the personnel director, in writing, whether or not an employee has satisfactorily completed his probationary period.
313: During the probationary period, the department head may remove an employee with or without cause. The department head shall immediately report the removal to the personnel director, and to the employee and shall state his reasons. Employees serving their probationary period do not have appeal rights unless there is alleged discrimination because of political affiliation age, race, color, creed, sex, religion, national origin, ancestry or disability.
314: The probationary period shall be used in connection with promotional appointments in the same manner as it is used for entrance appointments. If an employee is removed from his position during his probationary period following a promotion, he shall be entitled to his former position.
315: Separations of employees from positions in the classified service shall be designated as one of the following and shall be accomplished in the manner indicated: Resignation, compulsory resignation, layoff, disability, death, retirement and dismissal.
316: At the time of separation and prior to final payment, all records, assets and other items of city property in the employee's custody shall be transferred to his department head and certification to this effect shall be signed by the employee. Any amount due because of shortage in the above shall be withheld from the employee's final compensation.
317: Employees who separate shall receive payment for all earned salary and certify compensatory time subject to deductions as outlined in section 4-1056 of this chapter, and those employees who have completed their probationary service shall also receive payment for all earned annual leave.
318: To resign in good standing, an employee shall give notice, in writing, to his department head at least ten (10) working days prior to the effective date of his resignation. Normally, failure to comply with this rule shall be entered on the service record of the employee, and may result in a deduction from accrued vacation pay.
319: Any employee who without valid reason fails to report to work for three (3) consecutive work days without authorized leave shall be separated from the payroll and reported as a compulsory resignation.
320:
The city manager may identify numbers of positions by job title to be vacated which will result in the layoff of an employee in the classified service when he deemed it necessary because of shortage of funds or work, or other material changes in the duties or organization or for related reasons which do not reflect discredit upon the service of the employee. When any positions so vacated are refilled within a period of two (2) years following a layoff, the persons removed therefrom, if available and able to efficiently perform the duties of such positions, shall be first entitled to be restored to the position. The layoff of employees shall be made in inverse order, on the basis of length of service in the job title.
(Ord. No. 011-04, § 1, 4-19-04)
321: An employee may be separated for disability when he cannot perform the required duties, or when continuance on the job is a danger to himself or others. Action may be initiated by the employee at his expense, or the city at its expense, but in all cases, it must be supported by medical evidence acceptable to the city manager. An employee agrees upon request by the city, to submit to examination by a doctor of the city's choice and agrees to cooperate fully with the examination.
322: When a full time employee dies while in the service of the city, all compensation due in accordance with section 4-1057 of this chapter shall be paid to the legal representative of the employee's estate or any other properly designated individual.
323:
(a) When an employee meets the conditions of retirement set forth in the employees' retirement system, he or she may, after providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice of intent to retire, retire, and shall receive such compensation due in accordance with the provisions of sections 4-1057 and 4-1078(f) of this chapter. To the extent any employee's notice of intent to retire is less than the minimum amount prescribed above, the amount by which such employee's notice violates the above minimum time frame shall be reduced or deducted from any entitled compensation pursuant to the provisions of sections 4-1057 and 4-1078(f).
(b) The minimum time frames for notice of intent to retire prescribed in (a) above may be waived or reduced in the sole discretion of the city.
(Ord. No. 837-83, § 1, 3-9-83)
324:
The city manager may dismiss an employee for cause as outlined in section 4-1066 of this chapter. The employee shall be furnished notice of dismissal in writing, stating the reasons and the employee's right to answer the charge, and the employee's right to appeal as provided in section 4-1013 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 010-08, § 2, 3-17-08)
325:
The following provisions shall govern disciplinary actions affecting employees in the classified service. A department head, subject to the appeal rights of the employee, shall have the following alternatives for disciplinary action:
(1) A department head may submit a written reprimand to an employee, when an oral warning has not resulted in the expected improvement; or when more severe initial action is warranted. Copies shall be filed with the personnel director and the city manager.
(2) A department head may, for cause, suspend without pay an employee in his department for up to ten (10) days. A written statement specifically setting forth reasons for suspension shall be furnished to the employee. Copies shall be filed with the personnel director and the city manager. With the prior approval of the city manager, the length of the suspension may be extended.
(3) With the prior approval of the city manager, a department head may reduce the salary of an employee within the range provided in the pay plan or demote the employee for cause to a lower class. A written statement of the reasons for the action shall be furnished to the employee. Copies shall be filed with the personnel director and the city manager.
(Ord. No. 871-85, § 2, 1-22-85)
327: If determined to be in the best interest of the city, a nondepartment head supervisor may relieve an employee from duty for disciplinary purposes. Relief from duty shall be only from the time the action is initiated by the supervisor until the beginning of the employee's next scheduled work period. The supervisor shall report the action and circumstance to the department head who shall review the action and initiate any further disciplinary action which may be warranted.
328: The most effective accomplishment of the work of the city requires prompt consideration and equitable adjustment of employee grievances. It is the desire of the city to adjust grievances informally and both supervisors and employees are expected to make every effort to resolve problems as they arise. However, it is recognized that there may be grievances which will be resolved only after a formal appeal and review. No employee shall be disciplined or discriminated against in any way because of use of the grievance procedure.
329: A "grievance" is a complaint made by an employee concerning the interpretation of these rules and regulations or departmental work rules or working conditions.
330: Editor's note— Ord. No. 010-08, § 1, adopted March 17, 2008, repealed former § 4-1070 in its entirety which pertained to appeals and derived from the following: Ord. No. 871-85, § 3, 1-22-85; Ord. No. 1181-94, § 2, 7-18-94; Ord. No. 1120-96, § 3, 2-5-96.
331:
(a) An employee shall first present his grievance to his immediate supervisor who shall make careful inquiry into the facts and circumstances of the complaint. The supervisor shall attempt to resolve the problem promptly and fairly.
(b) An employee who is dissatisfied with the decision of his supervisor may submit his grievance, in writing, to his department head. The department head shall make a separate investigation and inform the employee, in writing, of his decision and the reasons for it within five (5) working days after receipt of the employee's grievance.
(c) If the employee is dissatisfied with the department head's decision, he may obtain a review by the city manager by submitting a request, in writing, within five (5) working days following the receipt of the department head's decision. The city manager shall make such investigation and conduct such hearings as he deems necessary and shall, within ten (10) working days after the receipt of the employee's request for review, inform the department head and employee, in writing, of his findings and decision.
(d) The employee shall have the right, at all levels, to a closed hearing and may be represented at the hearing.
332: Editor's note— Ord. No. 1120-96, § 4, adopted Feb. 5, 1996, repealed former section 4-1072 in its entirety which pertained to the appeal of disciplinary action and derived from this codification.
333: The hours of operation for each department shall be established by the department head with the approval of the city manager. The work schedule shall be placed on file with the personnel office and it will be the responsibility of the department head to notify the personnel office of any changes.
334:
(a) Overtime. Department heads are authorized to grant overtime at the rate of time and one-half (½) when the work being performed is mission critical or as required by law. Any overtime which is not pre-authorized by action of city council must be justified in writing as mission critical. Overtime is paid after forty (40) hours per week for all general employees and police personnel. Overtime is paid after two hundred twelve (212) hours in the designated twenty-eight-day work period for fire sworn personnel as in accordance with the Fair Labor Standards Act 207(k) exemption.
(1) Mission critical. Mission critical overtime is defined as overtime necessary to prevent disruption of essential city services. These services include but are not limited to the following:
a. Sewer or waterline breaks during non-working hours of assigned crews.
b. Power-outages as a result of tree limbs, broken poles, storm damage, etc.
c. Storm-related emergencies for sanding of streets, clearing roadways, or restoring basic city services.
d. Shortage of manpower which necessitates calling in personnel to prevent the closing down of emergency equipment.
e. Shortage of manpower which necessitate calling in additional personnel to prevent the reduction of emergency services.
f. Street or bridge cave-ins or collapse which would effect the safety of the public.
g. Seasonal leaf pick-up when determined that not working overtime would disrupt collection schedules.
h. Revenue critical functions needed to maintain cash-flow and schedule of hearing mandates in the area of court services.
(2) Legal requirements.Under federal law, fire personnel must be paid overtime after an average of fifty-three (53) hours per week of work time. This does not sufficiently cover the hours to maintain a twenty-four-hour operation. When minimal staffing levels to do not allow time off, overtime will be paid to meet federal guidelines.
(3) Assignment of overtime.
a. Assignment of overtime must be managed such that the work is performed by the least number of employees needed to accomplish the task required, and should be performed by the employees at the lowest rate of pay who have the required skills and experience to perform the mission critical tasks.
b. Overtime paid per employee must be documented with justification for the overtime as mission critical, and this documentation must be made available upon request for management review.
(b) Compensatory time.
(1) For employees hired on or after September 1, 2002, compensatory time, or time off in lieu of overtime, may be granted for overtime hours worked. These hours worked over the maximum regular hours allowed in each work period (forty (40) hours for employees except fire personnel) will be accrued at the rate of time and one-half (½) of the employee's regular pay rate. For employees hired before September 1, 2002, compensatory time may be taken in place of overtime at the employee's discretion.
(2) Employees who accrue overtime earned as comp-time may be required to take comp-time at a time when city services will not be seriously affected, as determined by the department head. The maximum accrued comp-time per employee is two hundred forty (240) hours for general employees and four hundred eighty (480) hours for fire and police personnel. All overtime earned after the maximum comp-time accrual is reached must be paid as overtime pay. Any accrued and unused comp-time must be paid in full when the employee ceases to be employed by the city.
(Ord. No. 805-82, § 1, 9-7-82; Ord. No. 024-02, §§ 1, 2, 9-3-02)
335:
The following days are designated as holidays: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, the first Tuesday following the first Monday in November ("Election Day"), Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day. When Christmas Day and New Year's Day falls on a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday employees shall receive one day leave on Christmas Eve and one-half-day leave on New Year's Eve. Other work days may be declared holidays by the mayor and council at their discretion. When a holiday falls on Saturday, the preceding Friday shall be observed as the holiday. When a holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday shall be observed as the holiday.
(Ord. No. 1046-93, § 1, 2-1-93; Ord. No. 1161-98, § 1, 7-6-98; Ord. No. 025-02, § 1, 9-3-02; Ord. No. 129-019, 11-4-19; Ord. No. 161-020, 7-20-20)
336:
Employees shall be eligible for pay for all city designated holidays.
(Ord. No. 025-02, § 1, 9-3-02; Ord. No. 008-014, § 1, 5-19-14)
337:
The employees required to work the holiday shall be compensated at the pay rate of time and one half for having worked the holiday.
(Ord. No. 025-02, § 1, 9-3-02; Ord. No. 008-014, § 1, 5-19-14)
338:
Any period of absence occurring on a scheduled work day immediately prior to or immediately subsequent to a designated holiday or a furlough day will require a medical certificate signed by a licensed physician to substantiate the leave request in order to receive compensation for the period of absence. This requirement will apply to all absences except pre-approved annual or personal leave.
(Ord. No. 025-02, § 1, 9-3-02; Ord. No. 008-014, § 1, 5-19-14)
339: Part-time employees shall not be paid for observed holidays which are not worked.
340:
All regular full time employees employed after July 21, 1980, shall accrue annual leave at the rate of .833 days per month, or ten (10) days per year; and all employees employed prior to July 22, 1980, shall accrue leave at the rate of one day per month, or twelve (12) days per year.
After completing four (4) years service, annual leave shall be accrued at the rate of one and twenty-five hundredths (1.25) days per month, or fifteen (15) days per year.
After completion of fourteen (14) years of service, annual leave shall be accrued at the rate of one and sixty-one hundredths (1.61) days per month, or twenty (20) days per year.
After completion of nineteen (19) years of service, annual leave shall be accrued at the rate of two and eight hundredths (2.08) days per month, or twenty-five (25) days per year.
(Ord. No. 822-82, § 2, 12-13-82)
341:
(a) Sick leave with pay shall be granted to regular, full time employees only in the case of: actual sickness or disability of the employee, or the employee's immediate family member, resulting from causes beyond the employee's control; or medical or dental examinations or treatments for which arrangements cannot be made outside of working hours.
(1) For purposes of this section "immediate family member" means an employee's child, spouse, grandchild, grandparent, parent, or any dependents as shown in the employee's most recent tax return.
(b) The employee shall report to his supervisor the reason for his use of sick leave prior to his schedule work time if possible. If this is not possible, he shall see that his absence is reported within thirty (30) minutes after the time he is scheduled to report for work. Failure to do so may be cause for denial of sick leave with pay for that day and for each subsequent day that prior notification has not been given. Special consideration will be given to emergency situations.
(c) A medical certificate signed by a licensed physician will be required by the department head to substantiate leave requests or sick leave for the following reasons:
(1) Any period of absence consisting of three (3) or more consecutive days.
(2) Sick leave of any duration if absence from duty recurs frequently or habitually provided that an employee has been notified that a certificate will be required.
(3) Any period of absence occurring on a work day prior to or subsequent to a holiday as defined in this chapter.
(d) Full-time employees begin to accrue sick leave immediately upon employment at the rate of one day per month. Sick leave may not be taken in increments smaller than one-half of a day. No sick leave may be taken beyond that which is already accrued.
(e) Unused sick leave may be carried into the next calendar year, on an unlimited basis.
(f) Sick leave compensation upon retirement.
(1) Employee shall not be compensated upon retirement for unused sick leave accumulated after December 31, 1978.
(2) Employees who, upon retirement from their employment freeze their retirement benefits, shall not be paid for any accumulated unused sick leave.
(3) Employees on the payroll prior to December 12, 1977, shall be paid upon retirement for all unused sick leave accumulated and recorded in the personnel office through December 31, 1978; less sick leave taken which exceed unused sick leave accumulated after December 31, 1978. Payment for accumulated sick leave shall be by continuation of salary until said accumulated sick leave has been paid and commencement thereafter of any pension entitlements of said retiring employee.
(4) Employees hired after the adoption of these rules and regulations shall not be compensated for accumulated unused sick leave upon retirement.
(Ord. No. 845-83, §§ 1, 2, 5-2-83; Ord. No. 1113-95, § 1, 7-3-95; Ord. No. 081-017, 11-20-17)
342: Editor's note— Ord. No. 881-85, § 1, adopted June 3, 1985, deleted § 4-1079, pertaining to on the job injury leave, which section did not contain history notation.
343:
Employees are covered under the provisions of worker's compensation law. If an employee is injured while on the job, such an injury must be reported to the supervisor immediately.
(Ord. No. 1042-92, § 1, 10-5-92)
344: Funeral leave of up to three (3) working days shall be granted, with pay, for employees in the event of death in the immediate family. Immediate family shall mean husband, wife, son, daughter, brother or sister. For the purposes of this provision, immediate family is defined to include those members set forth herein previously together with mother, father, grandmother or grandfather of an employee or his or her spouse.
345:
(a) Any permanent employee who leaves the service of the city to join the military forces of the United States during time of war or other national emergency, or is inducted by selective service, may upon written request prior to his induction into the military, be placed on military leave without pay, such leave to extend through a date ninety (90) days after he is relieved from the military service. Such an employee shall be entitled to be restored to the position which he vacated, provided he makes application within ninety (90) days of the date of honorable discharge or discharge under honorable conditions and if physically and mentally capable of performing the work of his position.
(b) An employee who is a member of the National Guard or an organized military reserve of the United States will be allowed leave of absence not to exceed fifteen (15) calendar days during any calendar year to attend training camp upon presentation of orders pursuant to the training. The city shall pay the employee any difference in the amount received for the military service and the employee's regular salary.
346: An employee shall be given the time off with pay for jury duty or when subpoenaed to appear before any public body or commission.
347:
Leave of absence without pay may be granted to an employee upon his department head's recommendation, by the city manager for a period not to exceed six (6) consecutive months. No accrual privileges or benefits are allowed for an employee who is on leave of absence. Consideration for leave without pay will be given for reasons such as personal illness or disability of a member of the employee's household, or continuing education. The needs of the city will be the controlling factor.
When an employee is precluded from meeting the responsibility of the position to which he/she is assigned, because of being hurt off the job, personal illness, pregnancy, disability of a family member, physical limitation due to drugs, alcohol or physician's orders, leave of absence may be granted as set forth above, and when such leave of absence is granted, the employee shall pay the city's share of the employee's health and accident and life insurance.
(Ord. No. 838-83, § 1, 3-9-83)
348: The personnel director, under the direction of the city manager, shall be responsible for the development and promotion of inservice training of employees in order to improve the quality of city service and to assist employees in preparing themselves for advancement in the city employment.
349: An employee who enters a job related training program with the prior approval of his department head and the city manager may be reimbursed for expenses such as tuition and books upon successful completion of the program. Approval may be dependent on budget allocations. An expense advance may be issued if recommended by the department head and approved by the city manager.
350: The personnel director, under the direction of the city manager, and in cooperation with department heads, shall establish a system of service ratings based on standards of performance. The primary purpose of service ratings shall be to discuss with employees how they are performing on their job, and how their work performance could be improved. Department heads or supervisors shall review service ratings with employees, but the ratings shall be confidential between the supervisor, the department head, the employee and the personnel director.
351: It is the responsibility of the city to provide safe working conditions, tools, equipment and work methods for employees. All employees shall use the safety equipment provided, and shall follow all safety rules and safe working methods. Violation of safety rules shall be considered the same as violation of any departmental rule, and an employee in violation may be subject to disciplinary action.
352: Any on the job accident or injury shall be reported immediately to the supervisor. It is the responsibility of the supervisor to arrange for prompt medical attention if such is necessary, and to complete and submit a written report of the accident to the personnel director and his department head.
353: Editor's note— Ord. No. 001-05, § 1, adopted Jan. 18, 2005, repealed former section 4-1090 in its entirety. Former section 4-1090 pertained to an code of ethics incorporated by reference and derived from Ord. No. 1159-98, § 1, adopted April 20, 1985.
354:
All city employees working in the police, fire and communications departments and all city department heads are required to have a working telephone at their place of residence. All such employee's telephone numbers shall be reported to the personnel office by the respective employees. Also, any change in such telephone number shall be reported to the city manager's office by the affected employee within ten (10) days following such change.
(Ord. No. 1053-93, § 1, 7-6-93)

356:
Footnote 3:
Editor's note— An amended and restated retirement plan was issued by the city council and became effective on Jan. 1, 2001. This plan replaced former §§ 4-1101—4-1117 which pertained to the former retirement plan and derived from Ord. No. 1106-95, § 1, 6-5-95; Ord. No. 1157-98, §§ 1—6, 9, 5-18-98; Ord. No. 003-00, § 1, 12-6-99.
Charter reference— Retirement benefits, § 4-501.
357:
(a) Background. The plan initially was adopted and effective June 19, 1975 and subsequently amended and restated at various times. The plan, as set forth in this document, is intended and should be construed as a restatement and continuation of the plan as previously in effect. This restatement is intended to (i) consolidate various amendments made to the plan since the last restatement, (ii) clarify and modify certain provisions of the plan, and (iii) bring the plan into compliance with laws and regulations enacted or issued prior to the effective date of this restatement.
(b) Purpose. The primary purpose of the plan is to recognize employees' contributions to the operations of the City of East Point and to reward the same by providing eligible employees with an opportunity to accumulate a retirement benefit for their future security and that of their beneficiaries.
(c) Type of plan. The plan is intended to be a governmental defined benefit pension plan qualified under Section 401(a), with the related trust qualified under Section 501(a), of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
(d) Applicability of amendment. The plan is hereby amended, and adopted by the city council, effective October 20, 2003. Any person who is covered by the plan as in effect before October 20, 2003, and who retired or otherwise terminated employment before October 20, 2003, shall continue to be entitled to the rights and benefits, if any, provided under the plan as in effect on his retirement or termination of employment.
The accrued benefit of an eligible employee who is a participant in the plan as of October 20, 2003, shall not in any circumstances be less than the participant's accrued benefit as of October 19, 2003, determined under the terms of the prior plan as in effect on October 19, 2003.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, Art. 1; Ord. No. 003-04, 2-2-04)
358:
For purposes of the plan, the following terms, when used with an initial capital letter, shall have the meanings set forth below unless a different meaning plainly is required by the context.
Accrued retirement benefit means the pension benefit to be provided for each participant (other than city council) commencing on the first day of the month next following his actual retirement date. This is payable during the participant's lifetime, with seventy-five (75) percent continued to a qualified spouse, or children until age eighteen (18), in a monthly amount equal to (a) times (b) times (c), where:
(a) is the applicable benefit percentage,
(b) is the years of credited service, and
(c) is the average monthly compensation.
The child's benefit shall continue to age twenty-four (24) if the child is a full-time student. It will be reduced fifty (50) percent and continued for the life of the child if, in the sole discretion of the pension board, the child is handicapped and unemployable.
Actuarial equivalent means amount is the actuarial equivalent of any other amount if the actuarial reserve required to provide the same is equal to the actuarial reserve required to provide such other amount.
(1) Optional payment forms other than lump sum. This is computed on the basis of the 1983 Group Annuity Mortality Table blended eighty (80) percent male and twenty (20) percent female, and an annual interest rate of seven (7).
(2) Lump sum distributions. (A lump sum payment does not reduce the seventy-five (75) percent survivor's benefit.) This is computed on the basis of the interest rates and mortality tables specified by Section 417(e)(3)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code, as follows:

(b) Disability: "Disability" means Social Security Disability, if eligible, or if not, a total and permanent physical or mental condition as defined by East Point's long term disability plan resulting from bodily injury, disease, or mental disorder which renders a participant incapable of continuing his usual and customary employment with the employer; provided, however, that disability for purposes of the plan shall not include any disability which results from the participant's engagement in war, insurrection, rebellion, or active participation in a riot, or in a criminal enterprise, or from an intentionally self-inflicted injury. These payments will cease if the participant does not qualify for Social Security Disability or East Point long term disability benefits within a period to be determined solely by the board. 376:
When a participant dies, all or a portion of his pension will be continued to a beneficiary as follows:
(1) Married participants: Upon a participant's death, the qualified spouse will automatically receive seventy-five (75) percent of his benefit until her death, with child benefits payable thereafter as per section 4-1102, definition of "actuarial equivalent." The married participant may elect option (2)d. below, but his qualified spouse's benefit will not be reduced.
(2) Participants without a qualified spouse or child: Upon retirement, or phased retirement, a single participant without a child may choose any of the following optional forms of benefit:
a. Joint and survivor option: A reduced benefit is paid to a participant; upon his death a percentage of that reduced benefit is continued to his beneficiary. A participant may elect that his beneficiary receive one hundred (100) percent, seventy-five (75) percent, fifty (50) percent or twenty-five (25) percent continuation.
b. Period certain and life option: A decreased benefit is payable for life, with payments guaranteed for the first five (5), ten (10), fifteen (15) or twenty (20) years as selected by the participant.
c. Social Security level income option: This option applies only if a participant is retiring before age sixty-two (62) and expects to receive a retirement benefit from Social Security. He may elect to receive an increased benefit at his retirement, which will be decreased when he starts to receive his Social Security benefit, so that the sum of his two (2) benefits will be roughly equal to the benefit he began receiving at initial retirement.
d. Lump sum option: On the date a participant attains early, normal, disability or late retirement, a participant may elect to receive either five (5) percent, ten (10) percent, fifteen (15) percent, twenty (20) or twenty-five (25) percent of his accrued benefit in a one-time lump sum based upon the present value under Code Section 417(e)(3)(A). The monthly benefit payable to the participant shall be reduced by the percentage elected. But any benefit payable to a surviving beneficiary shall not be reduced.
All options are null and void if the participant, or his beneficiary, dies before the annuity starting date.
Payments to married and single participants will at least equal the multiple of participant's contributions shown in subsection 4-1109(c)(2).
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 4.02; Ord. No. 003-04, 2-2-04)

Effective July 1, 1998, each participant shall contribute to the trust fund at an annual rate of six (6) percent of his compensation, by means of regular payroll deductions (hereinafter, the "participant contributions"). Effective July 1, 1998, the employer will pick up participant contributions. Such participant contributions will be treated as employer contributions in accordance with Internal Revenue Code Section 414(h) and any treasury regulations promulgated thereunder. Employer pick-up of participant contributions shall be effectuated by reducing the compensation of each participant by six (6) percent. No participant shall have the option to receive the pick-up contributions directly instead of having such contributions paid by the employer to the trust fund.
(b) Subject to section 4-1118(e), the employer shall contribute to the trust fund monthly such amounts as from time to time are estimated by the actuary to be sufficient, upon an actuarially sound basis, to provide the balance of accrued retirement benefits under the plan not provided by participant contributions and earnings.
(c) Effective July 1, 2001, the employer shall contribute to the trust fund at an annual rate of sixteen (16) percent of each participant's compensation or such other amount as recommended by the actuary and adopted by the employer. Such contributions may be made in cash or in property which is an authorized investment of the trust fund (as provided in the trust agreement) or in a combination of cash and such property.
(d) The expenses of administering the plan, including such items as the accounting, actuarial, legal, and trustee's fees, shall be paid by the trust fund.
(e) Notwithstanding anything contained herein to the contrary, the employer shall have the right in its sole and final discretion, at any time or from time to time, to discontinue or temporarily suspend for a definite or indefinite period, its contributions under the plan without any liability whatsoever. Upon the complete discontinuance of contributions by the employer, the rights of participants shall be nonforfeitable in accordance with and to the extent provided in subsection 4-1333(c).
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 5.02)
382:
(a) There is hereby established a pension board (board), whose duty it shall be to see that the provisions of the plan are carried out and that funds are kept separate and to act at all times in the best interest of the participants, plan and trust fund.
(b) Board membership.
(1) The board shall be composed of the following:
a. The City of East Point's Human Resources Director;
b. Two employee representatives elected by the active participants for terms of four (4) years;
c. One member of the East Point City Council to be appointed by the city council for a term of two (2) years;
d. One (1) member who shall be a resident of the City of East Point, with a preference for a resident with banking, insurance, and/or accounting experience and knowledge of pension and retirement fund matters, who shall be appointed by the city council for a term of four (4) years;
e. Two (2) retired employees elected by the retired participants for terms of four (4) years.
(2) Any board member elected by active participants or retirees, who misses three consecutive meetings, after being properly notified thereof, shall be replaced as a member at the next scheduled election.
(3) If a vacancy on the board occurs, and the term remaining of such vacating member is six (6) months or more, a special election shall be called by the board to fill the vacancy for the remainder of the expired term. If the term remaining is less than six (6) months, the vacancy shall be filled for the unexpired term by the remaining members.
If a member of the board who was appointed by the city council vacates his or her position, and there are more than six (6) months remaining before the term of such member expires, the city council shall appoint a person to fill the vacancy for the remainder of the unexpired term.
(4) Each member shall, within ten (10) days after appointment or election, take an oath of office, affirming that he or she will diligently and honestly administer the affairs of the board, and will not knowingly violate or willingly permit to be violated any laws applicable to the trust fund or provisions herein. The oath shall be subscribed to the member certified by the person authorized to administer the oath and filed with the city clerk.
(5) Should an elected or appointed member of the board, except as otherwise provided herein, retire, resign, or otherwise become unable to perform as a member of the board before his term of office expires, the office of such member shall be declared vacant and shall be filled as provided above.
(6) The board shall be authorized to make all necessary rules in carrying out the provisions of the plan relative to electing members to the board; provided, however, that the names of candidates in any election shall be sent to those persons eligible to vote not more than forty-five (45) days nor less than thirty (30) days before said election.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.01; Ord. No. 010-05, § 1, 6-6-05; Ord. No. 003-13, 3-4-13)
383:
The board shall act by agreement of a majority of its members, either by vote at a meeting or in writing without a meeting. By such action, it may authorize one (1) or more of its members or the plan administrator to execute documents on its behalf and direct the trustee in the performance of its duties, as related to the powers and duties of the board specified below; and the trustee, upon written notification of such authorization, shall accept and rely upon such documents and directions until notified in writing that the authorization has been revoked or changed by the board. A member of the board who is also a participant shall not vote or act upon any matter directly affecting any of his benefits under the plan. In the event of a deadlock or other situation which prevents agreement of a majority of the board members, the matter shall be decided by the city council.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.02)
384:
The board shall have the power and duty to do all things necessary or convenient to affect the intent and purposes of the plan and not inconsistent with any of the provisions hereof whether or not such powers and duties are specifically set forth herein and, not in limitation but in amplification of the foregoing, shall have power to:
(1) Provide rules and regulations for the administration of the plan, and from time to time, to amend or supplement such rules and regulations.
(2) Construe the plan and/or trust agreement and its construction thereof in good faith, and act in the best interests of the participants.
(3) Correct any defect or supply any omission or reconcile any inconsistency in the plan in such manner and to such extent as it shall deem expedient to carry the same into effect.
(4) Determine all questions that shall arise under the plan including directions to and questions submitted by the trustee on all matters necessary for it to properly discharge its duties; provided, however, that in no event shall the board have any authority to direct any money manager or the trustee in the investment of the trust fund.
(5) The board shall select a custodian who will issue all benefit and expense payments.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.03)
385:
(a) Participants and beneficiaries shall apply for benefits by filing with the plan administrator a signed, written request specifically identifying the benefits requested and describing all facts and circumstances entitling the applicant to payment.
Each participant and beneficiary, or his representative, shall be responsible for making application, in accordance with uniform procedures established by the board, for any benefit due him under the plan.
(b) Within ninety (90) days after receipt of such an application, the plan administrator shall notify the applicant of the board's decision. If special circumstances require an extension of time, the plan administrator shall notify the applicant of such circumstances within ninety (90) days after receipt of the application, and the plan administrator shall thereafter notify the applicant of its decision within one hundred eighty (180) days after receipt of the application. If the application is denied in whole or in part, the plan administrator's notice of denial shall be in writing and shall state:
(1) The specific reasons for denial with specific reference to pertinent plan provisions upon which the denial was based;
(2) A description of any additional materials or information necessary for the applicant to perfect his or her claim and an explanation of why the materials or information are necessary; and
(3) An explanation of the plan's claim review procedure.
(c) During the sixty-day-period following an applicant's receipt of a notice of denial of the application for benefits, the applicant or a duly authorized representative may review pertinent documents and within sixty (60) days submit a written request to the plan administrator for the board's review of the denial.
An applicant submitting a request for review shall be allowed to submit issues and comments in writing to the plan administrator. Within sixty (60) days after receipt of the request for review, the plan administrator shall issue the board's decision in writing to the applicant. If special circumstances require an extension of time, the plan administrator shall notify the applicant of such circumstances within sixty (60) days after receipt of the request for review, and the plan administrator shall issue the board's decision in writing no later than one hundred twenty (120) days after receipt of the request for review. The plan administrator shall include specific reasons for the board's decision, written in a manner calculated to be understood by the applicant, and contain specific references to the pertinent plan provisions upon which the decision is based.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.04)
386:
(a) The board will elect a chairman and secretary.
(b) The board may appoint such advisors as follows:
(1) Retaining advisors. The board shall have the right to hire such professional advisors as it, in its sole discretion, deems necessary or advisable. To the extent that the costs for such advisors are not paid by East Point, they shall be paid, at the discretion of the board, from the fund as an expense of the fund.
(2) Reliance on advisors. The board shall be entitled to rely upon all certificates and reports made by an actuary, accountant or attorney selected pursuant to this section. The board and East Point shall be fully protected in respect to any action taken or in good faith in reliance upon the advice or opinion of any such actuary, accountant or attorney. Any action so taken or suffered shall be conclusive upon each of them and upon all other persons interested in the plan.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.05)
387:
The board shall appoint a plan administrator to handle administrative details of the plan that the board chooses to delegate to the plan administrator. The plan administrator shall serve at the pleasure of the board.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.06)
388:
The duties of the plan administrator shall include, but not be limited to the following:
(1) Notification to participants: The plan administrator shall help East Point notify each employee of his participation in the plan within thirty (30) days of his participation starting date and annually thereafter by benefit statements.
(2) Information to actuary: The plan administrator shall help East Point furnish the actuary such information as he may require to properly perform his duties.
(3) Certification of benefits: The plan administrator shall certify the retirement, disability, termination and death benefits payable under the plan.
(4) Maintenance of records: The plan administrator shall help East Point keep all records required to reflect the status of each participant properly, and make available to each participant the records of his status in the plan.
(5) Direct benefit payments: The plan administrator shall help East Point review the trustee database and direct the trustee to make benefit payments as required by the provisions of the plan, after approval by the board.
(6) Monthly board meetings: The plan administrator will attend all board meetings to discuss administrative issues.
(7) Money manager meetings: The plan administrator will accompany the board to periodic meetings with the money managers and trustee.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.07)
389:
No member of the board nor the plan administrator (for purposes of this section, references to "the board" shall be deemed to include the plan administrator) shall be directly or indirectly responsible or under any liability by reason of any action or default by him as a member of the board, or the exercise of or failure to exercise any power or discretion as such member, except for his own fraud or willful misconduct; and no member of the board shall be liable in any way for the acts or defaults of any other member of the board or any of its advisors, agents, or representatives. Without limitation or restriction upon any other indemnification right at law or otherwise, East Point shall indemnify and save harmless each member or former member of the board against any and all expenses and liabilities arising out of his membership on the board, except expenses and liabilities arising out of his own fraud or willful misconduct. The fact that any member of the board is a member of the city council, or employee of east point, or a participant, shall not disqualify him from doing any act or thing which the plan authorizes or requires him to do as a member of such board (except as otherwise provided in section 4-1120 with respect to a member who is a participant).
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.08)
390:
The members of the board shall serve without compensation for their services, and shall be entitled to receive reimbursement of their reasonable expenses incurred in administering the plan. Any such expenses shall be paid by the trust fund.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.09)
391:
East Point shall furnish to the board, in writing, such information as the board may request in the exercise of its powers and duties in the administration of the plan. Such information may include, but shall not be limited to, the Social Security numbers, names of employees, their compensation and dates of birth, employment, termination of employment, disability, retirement, or death. Such information shall be conclusive for all the purposes of the plan and the board shall be entitled to rely thereon; provided, however, that the board may correct any errors discovered in any such information.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.10)
392:
The board shall make available to each participant for examination by him, at the principal office of the employer, a copy of the plan and such of its records or copies thereof as may pertain to any benefits of such participant under the plan.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.11)
393:
In the exercise of any power or discretion under the plan or trust agreement, the board shall not take any action or direct the trustee to take any action in respect to any of the rights, benefits, or obligations of a participant under the plan which would be discriminatory in favor of some participants over others in substantially similar situations or under substantially similar sets of facts.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.12)
394:
Once each year, the board shall cause an audit to be made of the accounts and records of the trust fund by a firm of independent certified public accountants selected by the board. A copy of the audit report shall be furnished to the council, the board, the actuary, and the trustee.
(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 6.13)
396:
(a) The employer shall have the right, by action of the city council, in its sole and final discretion, to amend the plan from time to time, to any extent which the council may deem advisable; provided, however, that no amendment (other than an amendment required by the Internal Revenue Service as a condition of its approval of the plan and trust as qualifying under Sections 401(a) and 501(a) of the Internal Revenue Code) shall retroactively decrease the benefits accrued to any participant or increase the duties or responsibilities of the trustee without its written consent.

(Ord. eff. 1-1-01, § 7.01)
